slides.image_prompt: Dario Amodei waist-up, head slightly forward, eyes wide in pure shock and delight directly at camera — caught the instant he saw the output materialize. Right hand flat on a dark open laptop, screen blazing with cascading blue and violet particle arcs (no text, only curving light shapes and glowing streaks). The Claude logo exactly as in the reference image burns as large white neon on the dark studio wall behind him. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain. Accent: electric violet against deep charcoal.

slides.headline: 1) FEED CLAUDE REAL DESIGNS WITH MOBBIN MCP
slides.body: MengTo fed Claude real app screens instead of written descriptions. Mobbin MCP connects Claude Code to thousands of actual app layouts in seconds.
slides.image_prompt: Hands-only close, no faces: one hand holds a phone displaying a clean geometric app UI in cool blue (no text, only shape grids and color blocks), the other rests at a laptop keyboard whose screen glows with the same visual hierarchy rebuilt as a dark animated interface. Dark studio desk surface. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain. Accent: electric blue against dark charcoal.

slides.headline: 2) USE COLLECT UI AS CLAUDE'S VISUAL TARGET
slides.body: Collect UI posts the best interface designs online every day. Paste one link into Claude Code and it has a real finished design to build toward instead of inventing from nothing.

slides.headline: 3) PASTE KAGE'S CODE INTO CLAUDE FOR STUDIO MOTION
slides.body: Kage is an open-source animation project with pre-built effects already working. Paste its source into Claude Code and ask it to wrap your content in those effects.
slides.image_prompt: A dark monitor screen ablaze with electric green particle trails arcing in motion blur across pure black — no text, only looping streaks and glowing point clusters suggesting animation in motion. Three matte dark folder icons fanned across the charcoal desk beside the monitor, catching neon green spill. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain. Accent: electric green against charcoal black.

slides.headline: 4) POINT CLAUDE AT TOWERS FOR THE VISUAL FEEL
slides.body: Towers curates finished web projects by visual style. Share the URL and Claude reverse-engineers its color system and animation timing into your project.

slides.headline: 5) SKETCH YOUR LAYOUT IN SKETCHBOOK FIRST
slides.body: Sketch your layout in Sketchbook, upload the image, and Claude reads the structure directly. A 30-second sketch becomes a working page structure without you describing a single pixel.

slides.headline: 6) THE STARTING PROMPT THAT SETS EVERYTHING
slides.body: MengTo open-sourced three repos and every prompt he used across the full tutorial. Every site starts with one prompt that locks in the visual direction before Claude writes a single line.

caption:
Swipe through these 6 free tools and Claude Code builds the animated website for you

Mobbin MCP, Collect UI, Kage, Towers, Sketchbook, and the open-source starting prompt: the six resources from MengTo's viral 40-minute tutorial on building animated landing pages with Claude Code and Opus 5, taught in the exact order he uses them.

Designers used to spend weeks on a single landing page. Now the best ones point Claude at a real reference and get a moving site in an afternoon. These six tools are what the people doing it are quietly using.
